![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14184009/assets/320a45751b2e718c66bb721cfcd78a2d206f08a9998fbbffddb1581ee995cf34.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{∂D}x\,dy-y\,dx,$ where $D$ is the region shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=x.$ So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=1.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}x\,dy-y\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-(-1))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =2\cdot ({4}^{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot (16-4) \\  & =2\cdot 12 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14184009/assets/e9892ef4efa3481ad02f7b8e38f1bae1876b196627204521d011656010297281.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=16,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=6,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=4,
$$

where ${C}_{1}$ is oriented counterclockwise and ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ are oriented clockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14184009/assets/b20b2b911c2a417c26fa951d9b28efa296c265df25e9d06b635ef4846267b93b.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =16+6+4 \\  & =26.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ${∮}_{∂D}2y\,dx+4x\,dy,$ where $D$ is the region shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$

$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=2y$ and $Q(x,y)=4x.$ So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=4.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}2y\,dx+4x\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4-2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =2\cdot (6\cdot 4-{2}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot (24-4) \\  & =2\cdot 20 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ${∮}_{∂D}(1-4y)\,dx+(2+5x)\,dy,$ where $D$ is the annular region shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=1-4y$ and $Q(x,y)=2+5x.$ So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-4,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=5.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}dx+x\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5-(-4))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}9\,\text{d}A \\  & =9\,\text{Area}(D) \\  & =9\cdot (\pi \cdot {3}^{2}-\pi \cdot {2}^{2}) \\  & =9\cdot 5\pi  \\  & =45\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
